features.name: Home-page financial overview and module linkages
steps: The home page shows the current financial accounts, budgets, trend chart, and recent transactions
After adding a transaction the account balance, budgets, trend chart, and transaction list all change together
When switching between "All / Expenses / Income" the list and statistics are recomputed from real transaction data
features.expected: After adding a transaction the account balance, budgets, trend chart, and list must update in sync and be numerically consistent; switching between "All, Expenses, Income" only changes the statistics scope and must not modify or hide the raw transaction data.

features.name: Full lifecycle of a financial account
steps: Create a new Bank/Cash account
Set the name, color, and currency
It appears in the accounts section of the home page
After editing, all transactions and statistics still refer to the same account
When archiving/deleting, the related screens update in sync; the official app also supports account creation, editing, sorting, and archiving.
features.expected: After creation an account must appear on the home page and be usable as a transaction target; changing its name or color must not break the association with existing transactions; after archiving or deleting, the related transactions and statistics update in sync without leaving orphaned references.

features.name: Main account and multiple currencies
steps: Different accounts choose currencies such as USD, EUR, JPY, and CNY
Choose the main account
New transactions use the main account by default
Global aggregates are expressed in the base currency defined by the main account
After switching the main account the default account and base-currency semantics change in sync.
features.expected: The main account must be unique and determines the default transaction account and the global aggregation currency; after switching the main account, the aggregation basis and the default account change in sync; each account's balance is still kept in its own currency.

features.name: Account balance correction and account merging
steps: Use "Correct total balance" on an account

The account reaches the specified balance, but the difference is not wrongly counted as ordinary income/expense; after "merge accounts" the source account's transactions move to the target account and the aggregates and transaction counts are recalculated. The official documentation defines Balance Correction as a special type that affects the balance but does not count as regular income/expense.
features.expected: A balance correction must make the account balance equal the target value, and the difference must not count as income or expense; after merging accounts all transactions move to the target account, the source account no longer appears, and the total net worth stays unchanged.

features.name: Expense / income transaction lifecycle
steps: Tap +
Choose expense or income
Set the amount, date/time, title, category, etc.
Save
The transaction enters the corresponding month and account
After editing the amount/date/account all statistics are recomputed
After deletion the balance, budgets, and charts roll back in sync
features.expected: After a transaction is saved it must be reflected at the same time in the account balance, the corresponding month list, and the statistics; after editing the amount, date, or account all statistics are recomputed; after deletion the balance, budgets, and charts roll back completely.

features.name: Categories, subcategories, and frequently used titles
steps: Create/select categories such as Groceries, Dining, and Shopping
Categories have a default expense/income direction
Subcategories can be created
A recurring title can help reuse a category
After editing a category, historical transactions are still correctly associated; the official documentation makes clear that categories drive statistics and budgets.
features.expected: A category must carry an income or expense direction and filter transactions accordingly; subcategories should belong to a parent category and aggregate correctly in statistics; renaming or adjusting categories must not break the association with historical transactions.

features.name: Rich transaction information
steps: Besides the amount, a transaction can have a title, notes, and attachments
They are restored in the transaction details after saving
Modifying or removing attachments/notes does not change the amount or the category relationship
The field state stays correct when copying/editing a transaction
features.expected: Notes and attachments must persist with the transaction and be restored in the details; deleting an attachment must not change the amount, category, or account; copying a transaction should keep the reusable fields without creating duplicate records.

features.name: Transfers between accounts
steps: Transfer between two accounts
The source account decreases and the destination account increases
The system creates mutually linked outgoing/incoming records
Total net worth does not change out of nowhere because of an internal same-currency transfer

When editing the transfer relationship both sides stay consistent. The official documentation states that one transfer creates two Balance Correction transactions with a net of 0; for cross-currency transfers an exchange rate can also apply.
features.expected: A transfer must generate a paired record and change the source and destination accounts in sync; a same-currency transfer must not change total net worth or count as income or expense; editing one side must keep the other side consistent.

features.name: Upcoming / subscription / recurring transaction state machine
steps: Choose "upcoming / subscription / recurring" when creating a transaction
Unpaid future transactions do not count toward the completed total
When due or manually marked Paid it enters the real financial statistics
A recurring transaction generates the next-period instance
Skip and Paid produce different state results. The official documentation gives a clear description of this state machine.
features.expected: An unpaid upcoming transaction must not count toward the balance or completed statistics; after marking it Paid it must count and generate the next-period instance; Skip and Paid must produce different states and subsequent-instance results.

features.name: Transaction month navigation, search, and combined filtering
steps: Switch between months such as July/August/September on the transactions page
Only the current period's records are shown
Search by title
Then add filters such as account, category, income/expense, and date
The results represent the intersection of the conditions
After clearing part of the conditions they are recomputed immediately. The official documentation also explicitly supports multi-condition transaction search and filtering.
features.expected: Switching months must show only that period's transactions; multiple filters are intersected, and clearing any condition immediately widens the results; searching and filtering must not modify any raw transaction data.

features.name: Income/expense analysis and derived charts
steps: Create several income/expense transactions in different categories
The home trend chart, the account-detail donut chart, and the income/expense totals change with the data
Switching "Outgoing/Incoming" or "All/Expenses/Income" only changes the statistics scope and does not modify the original transactions
features.expected: Charts and income/expense totals must be aggregated from real transactions and change in sync with additions, edits, and deletions; switching the statistics scope only changes the view and must not modify or hide the raw transactions.

features.name: Creating an expense budget / savings budget
steps: Create a new budget
Choose an expense budget or a savings budget
Set the name, target amount, color, start date, and period
Save
The budget card shows the current period range and progress
At the next period it enters a new period according to the rules
features.expected: A budget must define the current period range by its configured start date and period and show progress; when the period ends it automatically enters a new period and resets the current progress; expense and savings budgets must each show progress in the correct direction.

features.name: "Added only" budget
steps: Create an Added Only budget
Ordinary transactions do not count by default
Explicitly select the budget when adding/editing a transaction
The budget progress increases

After removing the transaction from the budget the budget decreases while the account balance and the transaction itself stay unchanged. The official definition says this budget only counts manually added transactions.
features.expected: Ordinary transactions must not automatically count toward this budget; only explicitly linked transactions count; after removing the link the budget progress rolls back while the transaction and account balance must stay unchanged.

features.name: "All transactions" dynamic budget rules
steps: Create an All Transactions budget
Configure the included transaction types, accounts, and categories, and exclude categories
Afterwards any new transaction matching the rules counts automatically
Those that do not match do not count
After changing the filter the historical transaction set is re-evaluated.
features.expected: Transactions matching the filter rules must automatically count and those that do not match must not; after changing the filter the existing transaction set must be re-evaluated rather than only affecting new transactions; exclusion conditions should take precedence over inclusion conditions.

features.name: Real-time budget progress and spendable allowance
steps: A ¥1000 monthly budget
Add expenses such as ¥200 and ¥100
The used percentage and remaining allowance change in sync
"How much can still be spent/saved per day" is recalculated from the remaining amount and remaining days
After editing or deleting a transaction the chart, percentage, and daily suggestion are all recomputed together
features.expected: The used percentage must equal the ratio of current-period spending to the budget amount, and the remaining allowance is the difference between the two; the daily spendable amount is computed from the remaining allowance and remaining days; after a transaction change all three values are recomputed in sync.

features.name: Periodic budgets and history
steps: Recurring budgets such as monthly/weekly cross period boundaries
A new period resets the current progress while keeping past-period records
View the past periods' spending breakdown through the history entry
The current period and historical periods share the same budget definition. The official documentation states that periodic budgets repeat and past periods can be viewed as history.
features.expected: When a new period starts the current progress must reset to zero while past periods' spending and progress records remain viewable; historical and current periods share the same budget definition, and deleting a budget must handle history consistently.

features.name: Home-page module customization
steps: Open "Edit home page"
Enable/disable modules such as accounts, budgets, goals, income/expense, trends, spending charts, pie chart, heatmap, and transaction list
Drag to reorder
After returning to the home page it is arranged entirely according to the new structure
Data content is not deleted by hiding modules. The official documentation confirms that modules can be reordered and shown/hidden.
features.expected: The home page must render modules in the configured order and visibility, and hidden modules are no longer shown; the configuration must persist and be preserved after a restart; hiding a module must not delete the underlying data, and re-enabling it keeps the data intact.

features.name: Bill splitting
steps: Create a new bill
Add participant names
Add items and set prices and quantities
With "even split" enabled the amount is divided by the number of participants
Multiple items accumulate into the bill total
After changing an item's amount/quantity the individual shares and the allocated total are recomputed in sync
features.expected: An item's subtotal must equal unit price times quantity, and the bill total is the sum of the items; with even splitting each person's share is correctly allocated by headcount and the shares sum to the total; after modifying an item the individual shares are recomputed in sync.

features.name: CSV transaction import / export
steps: Export the existing transactions as CSV
Prepare columns such as date, amount, and category in an external or test file
Map the CSV columns to Cashew fields during import
Positive numbers become income and negative numbers become expenses
A missing main category can be created according to the rules
After the import, accounts and statistics update. CSV targets transaction migration and is not equivalent to a full app backup.
features.expected: The column mapping must determine where fields are written; positive numbers must create income and negative numbers expenses; after importing, account balances and statistics update with the new transactions; invalid rows should be skipped or reported rather than silently writing wrong data.

features.name: Full data-file backup and restore
steps: Create a local Cashew Data File
Afterwards change accounts, budgets, transactions, and settings
Import the old data file
The current database as a whole returns to the backup point in time

The home page, budgets, and statistics are rebuilt from the restored data. The official documentation states that this file is a direct copy of the database, that restoring overwrites the current data, and that its semantics differ from CSV partial data migration.
features.expected: A restore must overwrite the current database and return to the backup point in time, and changes made after the backup should not remain; the home page, budgets, and statistics must be rebuilt from the restored data; this file contains full data and differs semantically from CSV partial migration.
